knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathfrak P\) be a class of distributed optimization instances, \(\mathfrak A\) a class of algorithms, \(C_P(z)\geq0\) an instance-dependent accuracy certificate, and \(\kappa(P)\) a vector of objective, oracle, network, and initialization parameters.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A framework definition encompassing deterministic or probabilistic guarantees while requiring the regime and resource model to be explicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed performance guarantee is a tuple \(\Gamma=(\mathfrak P,\mathcal A,C,\mathcal R,\delta,U)\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathfrak P\) and budget vector \(r\in\mathcal R\), the output \(z_{P,r}\) produced by \(\mathcal A\) obeys \(\Pr\{C_P(z_{P,r})\leq U(\kappa(P),r,\delta)\}\geq1-\delta\). The resource vector may record local oracle calls, communication rounds, messages, scalars, bits, and memory. For deterministic guarantees, \(\delta=0\) and the inequality holds pointwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed performance-guarantee system specifies an instance class, algorithm, measurable accuracy certificate, resource accounting model, failure level, and upper-bound function. Uniformly over the instance class, the algorithm's output after a declared resource budget must satisfy the bound with at least the declared probability. Objective geometry, oracle access, network parameters, and initialization enter through the parameter vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall P\in\mathfrak P,\ \forall r\in\mathcal R:\ \Pr\{C_P(z_{P,r})\leq U(\kappa(P),r,\delta)\}\geq1-\delta\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: An \(\varepsilon\)-complexity guarantee is \(N_P(\varepsilon,\delta)=\inf\{r:U(\kappa(P),r,\delta)\leq\varepsilon\}\), with the infimum interpreted in the resource ordering.
special_cases_latex: Expected guarantees take the form \(\mathbb E[C_P(z_{P,r})]\leq U(\kappa(P),r)\).
A communication-only system uses a scalar budget \(r=R\) counting communication rounds.
immediate_consequences_latex: Two rate claims are comparable only after aligning their instance, certificate, probability, and resource conventions.
Network-independent notation does not imply network-independent performance; graph parameters may be components of \(\kappa(P)\).
boundary_notes: A bare asymptotic rate without quantified constants or parameter dependence is not a complete system.
Lower bounds require a separate quantified statement over algorithms and instances.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective-geometry regime of a distributed problem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F(x)=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)+r(x)\) on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space \(X\), where each agent stores \(f_i\) and \(r\) is an optional proper lower-semicontinuous regularizer. Let \(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification by analytic properties of the global and, when explicitly required, local objectives; network assumptions are not geometry assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An objective-geometry regime is a predicate \(\mathcal G(F;\theta)\) determined by quantified inequalities on \(F\), its local summands, or their differential/generalized-differential mappings. Canonical predicates include convexity \(F(y)\geq F(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle\), strong convexity with an added \((\mu/2)\|y-x\|^2\), \(L\)-smoothness \(\|\nabla F(x)-\nabla F(y)\|\leq L\|x-y\|\), growth conditions relating \(F(x)-F^*\) to \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\), and nonconvex stationarity measured by a residual \(S_F(x)\). The regime records which predicates hold and their constants \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective-geometry regime is the explicitly quantified collection of regularity and curvature conditions imposed on the distributed objective, together with their constants. It may classify the objective as convex, strongly convex, smooth, growth-conditioned, or nonconvex with a specified stationarity residual. Conditions on the aggregate objective and conditions on every local function are distinct and must be recorded separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G(F;\theta)\) is the collection of declared, quantified objective inequalities and their constants \(\theta\).
special_cases_latex: The smooth strongly convex regime records \((L,\mu)\) and condition number \(\kappa=L/\mu\).
The composite nonconvex regime may use \(S_F(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))\) or a proximal-gradient mapping.
immediate_consequences_latex: Changing the geometry predicate changes the admissible accuracy certificates and attainable rate families.
Global smoothness of \(F\) does not by itself imply uniform smoothness of every \(f_i\).
boundary_notes: Graph connectivity, spectral gap, and communication latency belong to network geometry, not objective geometry.
The definition classifies assumptions; it does not assert a convergence rate.

notation.meaning: Infimum or attained minimum value of F, as declared.
Constants attached to the geometry predicates.

knowledge_statements.title: General Convex Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The general convex regime assumes proper closed convex local objectives and an attained aggregate optimum, but no uniform curvature; distributed convergence requires both vanishing aggregate objective error and vanishing disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,d\in\mathbb N\). For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, define \(F=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\), and assume \(X^*:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^d}F(x)\ne\varnothing\). Write \(F^*:=\min_{x\in\mathbb R^d}F(x)\), without assuming any positive strong-convexity modulus. For a sequence \(x^k=(x_1^k,\ldots,x_m^k)\in\mathbb R^{md}\), define \(\bar x^k=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m x_i^k\) and \(D(x^k)=\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m\|x_i^k-\bar x^k\|^2\bigr)^{1/2}\). Distributed convergence in this regime requires \(F(\bar x^k)-F^*\to0\) and \(D(x^k)\to0\).
assumptions_latex: \(m,d\in\mathbb N\).
Each \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}F\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(\bar x^k)-F^*\to0\) and \(D(x^k)\to0\) constitute distributed convergence in this regime.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex distributed objectives without assumed positive curvature.

notation.meaning: Euclidean consensus disagreement at index k.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let each \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and define \(F(x)=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)+r(x)\) with proper lower-semicontinuous convex \(r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex distributed optimization without assumed positive curvature, error bounds, or growth inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The problem is in the general convex regime when every \(f_i\) and \(r\) is convex, meaning \(h(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y)\leq\lambda h(x)+(1-\lambda)h(y)\) for every \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}h\) and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), and when \(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}F(x)\neq\varnothing\). No constant \(\mu>0\) is assumed to satisfy a strong-convexity inequality, and no error-bound or growth condition is included unless stated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed objective lies in the general convex regime when all declared local loss terms and the common regularizer are proper, lower-semicontinuous convex functions and the aggregate problem has a minimizer. The regime assumes neither strong convexity nor any substitute growth or error-bound condition. Smoothness and bounded subgradients are optional additional assumptions, not part of general convexity itself.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_i\in\Gamma_0(X)\ \forall i,\ r\in\Gamma_0(X),\ \operatorname*{argmin}F\neq\varnothing\), with no positive-curvature condition imposed.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For each convex \(h\) and \(x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial h\), \(h(y)\geq h(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle\) for every \(g\in\partial h(x)\) and \(y\in X\).
special_cases_latex: If \(r=\iota_C\) for a nonempty closed convex set \(C\), the model is constrained convex consensus optimization.
If every \(f_i\) is differentiable, convexity is equivalent to \(f_i(y)\geq f_i(x)+\langle\nabla f_i(x),y-x\rangle\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The solution set \(X^*\) is convex.
Uniqueness of a minimizer is not guaranteed.
boundary_notes: Local nonconvexity with a convex aggregate is excluded by this local-function formulation.
Lipschitz gradients, compact domains, and bounded subgradients require separate declarations.

notation.meaning: Proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions on X.

review_flags: The standard definition is mathematically routine, but no exact inspected source locator supports this distributed formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform quadratic curvature of the aggregate objective makes its constrained minimizer unique and bounds squared distance to that minimizer by objective error, while distributed convergence also requires consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,d\in\mathbb N\), let \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), and define \(F=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\). Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be convex and suppose \(F\) is proper and subdifferentiable at every point of \(X\). The problem is in the strongly convex regime with modulus \(\mu>0\) when, for every \(x,y\in X\) and every \(g\in\partial F(x)\), \[F(y)\ge F(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\frac{\mu}{2}\|y-x\|^2.\] If \(F\) attains its minimum over \(X\) at \(x^*\), then this minimizer is unique and \(F(x)-F(x^*)\ge(\mu/2)\|x-x^*\|^2\) for every \(x\in X\). Distributed convergence additionally requires all local copies to agree with \(x^*\).
assumptions_latex: \(m,d\in\mathbb N\) and \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is convex.
\(F=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\) is proper and subdifferentiable at every point of \(X\).
A minimizer \(x^*\in X\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}F(x)=\{x^*\}\) and \(F(x)-F(x^*)\ge\frac{\mu}{2}\|x-x^*\|^2\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributed objectives possessing uniform quadratic curvature.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space and \(F(x)=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)+r(x)\), where the terms are proper and lower semicontinuous and \(F\) is subdifferentiable on its effective domain.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global uniform strong convexity of the aggregate objective; local strong convexity is identified as a stronger optional condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mu>0\), the aggregate distributed objective is in the \(\mu\)-strongly convex regime when, for all \(x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial F\), \(g\in\partial F(x)\), and \(y\in X\), \(F(y)\geq F(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+(\mu/2)\|y-x\|^2\). The locally uniform version requires constants \(\mu_i\geq0\) satisfying the analogous inequality for each \(f_i\), with \(m^{-1}\sum_i\mu_i+\mu_r>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The strongly convex regime requires a uniform positive quadratic lower-curvature term in the subgradient inequality for the aggregate objective. This condition is global over the domain and yields a modulus \(\mu>0\). Requiring every local loss to have its own modulus is stronger than aggregate strong convexity and is therefore recorded separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(y)\geq F(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\frac\mu2\|y-x\|^2\quad\forall x,y,\ \forall g\in\partial F(x)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(F-(\mu/2)\|\cdot\|^2\) is convex.
The subdifferential is \(\mu\)-strongly monotone: \(\langle g-h,x-y\rangle\geq\mu\|x-y\|^2\) for \(g\in\partial F(x)\), \(h\in\partial F(y)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(F\) is differentiable, use \(g=\nabla F(x)\).
If each \(f_i\) is \(\mu_i\)-strongly convex and \(r\) is \(\mu_r\)-strongly convex, then \(F\) has modulus \(m^{-1}\sum_i\mu_i+\mu_r\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If a minimizer exists, it is unique.
boundary_notes: Restricted strong convexity and quadratic growth are weaker nearby regimes.
Strong convexity of the aggregate need not identify which agents contribute curvature.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hierarchy of objective growth and error-bound regimes
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, assume \(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}F\neq\varnothing\), and write \(F^*=\min F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global growth predicates around a nonempty solution set; distributed structure affects how the objective is evaluated but not these defining inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p\geq1\) and \(c>0\), \(F\) has \(p\)-order growth when \(F(x)-F^*\geq c\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^p\) for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}F\). Quadratic growth is the case \(p=2\). A residual mapping \(R:X\to X\) has a global error bound with constant \(\kappa>0\) when \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\leq\kappa\|R(x)\|\). For differentiable \(F\), the Polyak-Łojasiewicz regime with \(\mu>0\) is \((1/2)\|\nabla F(x)\|^2\geq\mu(F(x)-F^*)\). The hierarchy records exactly which of these predicates is assumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A growth-condition regime is specified by an inequality connecting objective error, distance to the solution set, or a stationarity residual. Power growth includes quadratic growth; an error bound controls solution distance by a residual; and the Polyak-Łojasiewicz condition controls objective error by gradient norm. These conditions can support faster rates without asserting strong convexity, so membership in each class must be stated independently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime is the declared subset of \(\{\text{power growth},\text{quadratic growth},\text{residual error bound},\text{PL}\}\) whose quantified inequalities hold globally.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Quadratic growth may be normalized as \(F(x)-F^*\geq(\alpha/2)\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^2\).
special_cases_latex: Strong convexity with modulus \(\mu\) implies quadratic growth with coefficient \(\mu/2\).
For constrained or composite models, \(R\) may be a projected-gradient or proximal-gradient mapping.
immediate_consequences_latex: The PL condition does not, by definition alone, require convexity.
A regime statement must identify whether its inequality is global or restricted to a sublevel set or neighborhood.
boundary_notes: No converse between strong convexity, quadratic growth, error bounds, and PL is asserted without additional hypotheses.
Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz exponents and local metric subregularity are nearby but distinct predicates.
review_flags: The hierarchy and nonimplication boundaries require an inspected authoritative source.
knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchy of objective growth and error-bound regimes
Error-Bound Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An error bound converts a computable first-order residual into distance from the aggregate solution set; distributed methods must still control disagreement separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex with nonempty minimizer set \(X^*\). An error-bound regime holds on a set \(U\subseteq\operatorname{dom}F\) if there exists \(\kappa>0\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le \kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))\qquad\text{for every }x\in U.\] The bound is local when \(U\) is a neighborhood of \(X^*\), and global when \(U=\operatorname{dom}F\). For distributed iterates, this condition controls optimization distance but does not replace a separate agreement residual.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}F\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))\) for every \(x\in U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-to-solution-distance bounds for convex aggregate objectives.

notation.meaning: Region on which the error bound holds.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The condition is a recognizable convex subdifferential error bound and fits the leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied. The plain statement should also avoid calling the residual computable without additional assumptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Dominance Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient dominance bounds aggregate objective error by squared gradient norm without requiring convexity; network disagreement remains a separate distributed residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable with finite attained minimum \(F^*\). The objective satisfies gradient dominance with constant \(\mu>0\) on \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) when \[\frac12\|\nabla F(x)\|^2\ge \mu\bigl(F(x)-F^*\bigr)\qquad\text{for every }x\in U.\] This condition does not require convexity. It ensures that a small gradient norm certifies small objective suboptimality on \(U\). In a distributed method, the gradient condition concerns the aggregate objective, while consensus error remains an additional quantity to control.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is differentiable on \(U\).
The finite value \(F^*\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x)-F^*\le (2\mu)^{-1}\|\nabla F(x)\|^2\) for every \(x\in U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyak–Łojasiewicz gradient dominance for smooth aggregate objectives.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The normalization and nonconvex interpretation of the Polyak–Łojasiewicz condition are mathematically standard, but the record has no source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Growth-Condition Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near the solution set, order-p growth implies every weaker order-q growth condition with q at least p; smaller exponents are stronger.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) have nonempty minimizer set \(X^*\), and suppose \(U\subseteq\operatorname{dom}F\) satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le1\) for every \(x\in U\). For \(p>0\), define order-\(p\) growth on \(U\) by \[F(x)-F^*\ge c\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^p\qquad(x\in U)\] for some \(c>0\). If this inequality holds with exponent \(p\), then it also holds with every exponent \(q\ge p\) on \(U\), using the same constant. Thus, on a normalized neighborhood, smaller exponents impose stronger growth.
assumptions_latex: \(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}F\ne\varnothing\).
\(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le1\) throughout \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\le q\) and order-\(p\) growth on \(U\) imply order-\(q\) growth on \(U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering of Hölderian objective-growth exponents near the solution set.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct ordering of powers on the unit neighborhood

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The exponent ordering on a unit neighborhood is correct and the property kind fits the hierarchy leaf, but no inspectable authoritative source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-versus-Global Growth
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global growth implies local growth, but the convex Huber function shows that local quadratic growth can coexist with merely linear behavior at infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A growth inequality is local if it holds only when \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le\delta\) for some \(\delta>0\), and global if it holds for every point in the domain. Every global inequality is local, but the converse fails. For example, the convex Huber function \[F(x)=\begin{cases}x^2/2,&|x|\le1,\\ |x|-1/2,&|x|>1\end{cases}\] has \(X^*=\{0\}\) and satisfies local quadratic growth with constant \(1/2\). No constant \(c>0\) makes \(F(x)\ge c|x|^2\) hold globally, because its growth is only linear as \(|x|\to\infty\).
assumptions_latex: Growth is measured relative to the nonempty minimizer set \(X^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local quadratic growth does not imply global quadratic growth, even for a finite convex function on \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local growth need not extend uniformly over the full domain.

notation.meaning: Radius of the local growth neighborhood.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit Huber counterexample is directly checkable

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The Huber example correctly separates local from global quadratic growth and the failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the counterexample and terminology lack an inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Nonconvex Stationarity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smooth distributed stationarity requires both a small aggregate gradient at the network average and small mean-square disagreement among agents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable and define \(F=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\). For local vectors \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\), set \(\bar x=m^{-1}\sum_i x_i\). The vector collection is an \(\varepsilon\)-stationarity certificate when \[\|\nabla F(\bar x)\|^2+\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m\|x_i-\bar x\|^2\le\varepsilon.\] The first term certifies approximate first-order stationarity of the aggregate smooth objective; the second certifies approximate agreement. A sequence reaches distributed stationary behavior when this combined quantity converges to zero.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is continuously differentiable.
All local vectors lie in \(\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla F(\bar x)\|^2+m^{-1}\sum_i\|x_i-\bar x\|^2\le\varepsilon\) certifies joint stationarity and agreement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order aggregate stationarity combined with network agreement.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The combined gradient-and-agreement quantity is a plausible certificate for this leaf, but the cited section supports graph consensus rather than the specific smooth nonconvex stationarity certificate and its normalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth Nonconvex Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsmooth nonconvex stationarity uses distance to the limiting subdifferential, while distributed stationarity also requires local variables to agree with the representative point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, possibly nonsmooth and nonconvex, and let \(\partial F\) denote its limiting subdifferential. A point \(u\in\operatorname{dom}F\) is \(\varepsilon\)-stationary when \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(u))\le\varepsilon.\] For distributed local vectors \(x_i\) and a representative \(u\), joint approximate stationarity and agreement require \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(u))^2+\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m\|x_i-u\|^2\le\varepsilon^2.\] The chosen subdifferential must be fixed explicitly because alternative nonsmooth stationarity notions need not coincide in nonconvex problems.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
\(\partial F\) is the limiting subdifferential.
\(u\in\operatorname{dom}F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(u))^2+m^{-1}\sum_i\|x_i-u\|^2\le\varepsilon^2\) is a joint stationarity–agreement condition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limiting-subdifferential stationarity with an explicit consensus residual.

notation.meaning: Limiting subdifferential of the aggregate objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Stationarity Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subgradient of the nonsmooth term certifies approximate stationarity when it nearly cancels the smooth gradient; the smallest such residual is the composite stationarity measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+r\) on \(\mathbb{R}^d\), where \(f\) is continuously differentiable and \(r\) is proper and lower semicontinuous. At any \(x\in\operatorname{dom}r\), a composite \(\varepsilon\)-stationarity certificate is a vector \(u\in\partial r(x)\) satisfying \[\|\nabla f(x)+u\|\leq\varepsilon.\] Equivalently, its optimal residual is \[\mathcal R_F(x):=\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\nabla f(x)+\partial r(x)\right)\leq\varepsilon.\] Here \(\partial r\) is the limiting subdifferential; thus the certificate remains meaningful when \(r\) is nonconvex.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuously differentiable.
\(r:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((x,u)\) certifies \(\mathcal R_F(x)\leq\varepsilon\); for \(\varepsilon=0\), it certifies \(0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial r(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order certificate for a smooth-plus-nonsmooth, possibly nonconvex composite objective.

notation.meaning: Limiting subdifferential of r at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth-Regularization Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even uniformly accurate smooth approximations can have stationary points whose original nonsmooth stationarity residual stays bounded away from zero for every positive smoothing parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(a\in(0,1)\). The nonsmooth objective \(F(x)=|x|-ax\) has \(0\in\partial F(0)\). Its smooth approximation \(F_\mu(x)=\sqrt{x^2+\mu^2}-ax\), with \(\mu>0\), satisfies \(\sup_x|F_\mu(x)-F(x)|\leq\mu\). Nevertheless, \(F_\mu\) has the stationary point \[x_\mu=\frac{a\mu}{\sqrt{1-a^2}}>0,\] while the original nonsmooth residual there is \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x_\mu))=1-a.\] Hence uniform value approximation and exact stationarity of the regularized problem do not imply vanishing stationarity residual for the original problem at finite \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Although \(F_\mu'(x_\mu)=0\) and \(F_\mu\to F\) uniformly, \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x_\mu))=1-a>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform smoothing accuracy does not preserve finite-parameter nonsmooth stationarity.

children.top_down_role: Rates for general convex, nonsmooth, and nonconvex regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Sublinear Distributed Rate Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed error belongs to a sublinear family when it decays polynomially; order p yields iteration complexity proportional to epsilon raised to minus 1/p.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_t\geq0\) denote a specified expected optimality, feasibility, consensus, or stationarity error after \(t\) distributed iterations. A method has a sublinear distributed rate of order \(p>0\) when constants \(C>0\) and \(t_0\geq0\) exist such that \[E_t\leq \frac{C}{(t+1)^p}\qquad\text{for all }t\geq t_0.\] Consequently, the iteration count sufficient for \(E_t\leq\varepsilon\) is \[t=O\!\left((C/\varepsilon)^{1/p}\right).\] The constant may depend on network connectivity, initialization, noise, and problem geometry; the exponent identifies the rate family.
assumptions_latex: \(E_t\) is a nonnegative, explicitly specified performance measure.
The bound holds uniformly for all \(t\geq t_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accuracy requirement \(E_t\leq\varepsilon\) is attained within \(O((C/\varepsilon)^{1/p})\) distributed iterations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomially decaying guarantees for distributed optimization error or stationarity measures.

notation.meaning: Chosen distributed performance error after iteration t.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a distributed method generate states \(X^k=(x_1^k,\ldots,x_n^k)\) for a problem with solution set \(X^\star\). Let \(E_k=E(X^k)\ge 0\) be a prescribed error functional, such as expected objective error, stationarity residual, feasibility violation, or consensus error.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic or expected stochastic rates are covered after the error functional and averaging convention have been fixed; the definition does not assert that any particular method attains such a rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family of distributed instances and algorithms has a sublinear rate of order \(p>0\) for \(E\) if, for every admissible instance, there exist finite constants \(C\ge0\) and \(k_0\in\mathbb N\) such that \(E_k\le C(k+1)^{-p}\) for all \(k\ge k_0\). The family is uniformly sublinear over an instance class when the same exponent \(p\) and a class-controlled bound on \(C\) apply throughout that class. More generally, a rate envelope \(r_k\downarrow0\) is sublinear relative to geometric decay when \(r_{k+1}/r_k\to1\), and the claim \(E_k=O(r_k)\) means \(\sup_{k\ge k_0}E_k/r_k<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed rate family is sublinear of order \(p>0\) when its specified error is eventually bounded by \(C/(k+1)^p\), with finite instance-dependent \(C\). Uniformity requires the exponent and constant control to hold across the declared instance class. The error, iterate convention, and whether the bound is deterministic or in expectation must be stated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists C<\infty,\ k_0\in\mathbb N\quad\forall k\ge k_0:\quad E_k\le \frac{C}{(k+1)^p}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For positive \(E_k\), the order statement is equivalent to \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}(k+1)^pE_k<\infty\).
An iteration complexity bound \(K(\varepsilon)=O(\varepsilon^{-1/p})\) follows when the envelope is monotone and \(K(\varepsilon)=\inf\{k:E_k\le\varepsilon\}\).
special_cases_latex: The choices \(p=1/2\), \(p=1\), and \(p=2\) give the standard \(O(k^{-1/2})\), \(O(k^{-1})\), and \(O(k^{-2})\) families.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every such rate implies \(E_k\to0\), but it need not imply convergence of each local state \(x_i^k\).
boundary_notes: Constants may depend on topology, initialization, smoothness, noise, and population size unless uniform independence is explicitly required.
A fixed nonzero noise floor is not a vanishing sublinear rate unless the error above the floor is used.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative distributed error measured at iteration or communication index \(k\).
First index at which the chosen error is at most \(\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Distributed Rate Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed method has a linear rate when its declared error contracts geometrically; reaching an accuracy below the initial bound requires logarithmically many additional iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_t\geq0\) be a specified distributed optimality-consensus error indexed by \(t\in\mathbb N_0\). A method has a linear distributed rate when constants \(C>0\), \(t_0\in\mathbb N_0\), and \(\rho\in(0,1)\) exist such that \[E_t\leq C\rho^{t-t_0}\qquad\text{for every }t\geq t_0.\] For any \(\varepsilon\in(0,C)\), the condition \[t\geq t_0+\left\lceil\frac{\log(C/\varepsilon)}{-\log\rho}\right\rceil\] is sufficient for \(E_t\leq\varepsilon\). In distributed methods, \(\rho\) may reflect both objective curvature or an error-bound constant and contraction of the communication operator.
assumptions_latex: \(E_t\) includes every error component required by the guarantee.
The target satisfies \(\varepsilon\in(0,C)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration complexity sufficient for \(E_t\leq\varepsilon\) is \(t_0+O\!\left(\log(C/\varepsilon)/(-\log\rho)\right)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric convergence under curvature, regularity, and contractive network mixing.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X^k=(x_1^k,\ldots,x_n^k)\) be distributed states and let \(E_k\ge0\) measure a fixed optimization, distance, feasibility, stationarity, or agreement error relative to the target set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition concerns geometric decay of a specified error. Curvature, error-bound regularity, and stable network mixing are typical sufficient conditions but are not built into the definition itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed method converges linearly for \(E\) on an admissible instance if there are \(C<\infty\), \(\rho\in(0,1)\), and \(k_0\in\mathbb N\) such that \(E_k\le C\rho^{k-k_0}\) for every \(k\ge k_0\). A family has a uniform linear rate on an instance class when one contraction factor \(\rho<1\) and class-controlled prefactor \(C\) work for all instances in that class. The definition is R-linear. Q-linear convergence is the stronger eventual one-step condition \(E_{k+1}\le\rho E_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear distributed convergence means eventual geometric reduction of the declared error: after some index, the error is at most a finite prefactor times a power of a contraction factor strictly below one. Uniform linear convergence requires class-wide control of that factor and prefactor. A direct one-step contraction is the stronger Q-linear variant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists C<\infty,\ \rho\in(0,1),\ k_0\in\mathbb N\quad\forall k\ge k_0:\quad E_k\le C\rho^{k-k_0}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The R-linear condition is equivalent to \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}E_k^{1/k}<1\) when finitely many zero terms are handled in the usual way.
Writing \(\rho=e^{-c}\) with \(c>0\) gives the exponential form \(E_k=O(e^{-ck})\).
special_cases_latex: If \(E_k=\|X^k-X^\star\|^2\), linear decay of squared distance corresponds to geometric decay of distance with factor \(\sqrt\rho\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The accuracy index satisfies \(K(\varepsilon)=O(\log(1/\varepsilon))\) when all other parameters are fixed.
boundary_notes: A contraction factor may depend on graph conditioning, objective curvature, step size, or delay bounds unless uniformity excludes that dependence.
Local linear convergence requires the initialization region to be included in the declared admissible class.
review_flags: The supplied source hints were not inspected to a locator establishing this exact R-linear and Q-linear taxonomy.

knowledge_statements.title: Network-Independent Asymptotic Rates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The distributed method is asymptotically network-independent when its leading decay scale and positive leading constant match the centralized reference, while graph-dependent effects are lower order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_t^{\mathrm{dist}}\) and \(E_t^{\mathrm{cent}}\) measure the same nonnegative error for a distributed method and its centralized reference, and let \(\phi(t)>0\) eventually with \(\phi(t)\to0\). The distributed guarantee is network-independent asymptotically when there is a constant \(C>0\), independent of the communication graph, such that \[E_t^{\mathrm{cent}}=C\phi(t)+o(\phi(t)),\qquad E_t^{\mathrm{dist}}=C\phi(t)+o(\phi(t)).\] Graph-dependent terms may occur at finite times but are lower order than \(\phi(t)\). Under these expansions, \[\frac{E_t^{\mathrm{dist}}}{E_t^{\mathrm{cent}}}\longrightarrow1.\]
assumptions_latex: Both errors use the same objective normalization and accuracy criterion.
\(\phi(t)>0\) eventually and \(\phi(t)\to0\).
The common leading constant \(C>0\) is independent of the communication graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The communication graph does not affect the leading asymptotic term, and \(E_t^{\mathrm{dist}}/E_t^{\mathrm{cent}}\to1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Leading-order distributed behavior matches the corresponding centralized performance law.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal G\) be an admissible class of connected communication networks. For each \(G\in\mathcal G\), let \(E_k(G)\ge0\) be the error of a distributed method, and let \(r_k\downarrow0\) be the benchmark envelope of a corresponding centralized method.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition separates the leading asymptotic term from a possibly network-dependent transient and lower-order remainder.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The distributed family has a network-independent asymptotic rate relative to \(r_k\) if there is a finite constant \(C_{\mathrm{lead}}\), independent of \(G\in\mathcal G\), such that for every fixed admissible network \(G\), \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}E_k(G)/r_k\le C_{\mathrm{lead}}\). A stronger uniform version requires \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\sup_{G\in\mathcal G}E_k(G)/r_k\le C_{\mathrm{lead}}\). Network dependence may remain in a finite burn-in index or in a remainder \(q_k(G)=o(r_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rate is network-independent asymptotically when, after normalization by the centralized benchmark rate, its leading limiting constant is bounded independently of the communication graph. This permits graph-dependent startup behavior and lower-order terms. Uniformity over graphs is stronger than taking the limit separately for each fixed graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists C_{\mathrm{lead}}<\infty\ \text{independent of }G\quad\forall G\in\mathcal G:\quad\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{E_k(G)}{r_k}\le C_{\mathrm{lead}}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A supported decomposition \(E_k(G)\le C_{\mathrm{lead}}r_k+q_k(G)\) with \(q_k(G)=o(r_k)\) implies the pointwise definition.
For \(r_k=k^{-p}\), the normalized condition is \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}k^pE_k(G)\le C_{\mathrm{lead}}\).
special_cases_latex: For stochastic methods, \(E_k(G)\) may be \(\mathbb E[F(\bar x^k)-F^\star]\), provided the expectation convention is fixed.
immediate_consequences_latex: Two networks may have the same leading asymptotic rate while requiring very different iteration counts to enter that regime.
boundary_notes: Pointwise independence does not imply a graph-uniform transient index.
If \(C_{\mathrm{lead}}\) contains a spectral gap or graph diameter, the rate is not network-independent under this definition.
review_flags: No inspected source locator supports the precise pointwise-versus-uniform asymptotic distinction used here.

knowledge_statements.title: Network-Dependent Transient Theory
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed error bound separates centralized and network-dependent terms, and the transient horizon is the first time after which the network term remains no larger than the centralized term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(t\in\mathbb N_0\). A network-dependent transient bound has the form \[E_t\leq A\phi(t)+B(\mathcal G,n,x^0)\psi(t),\] where \(A\phi(t)\) is a centralized-scale term, \(A>0\), and the finite coefficient \(B(\mathcal G,n,x^0)\geq0\) records the communication graph \(\mathcal G\), the number of agents \(n\), and the initialization \(x^0\). Suppose \(\phi(t)>0\) eventually and \(\psi(t)=o(\phi(t))\). Define \[T_{\mathrm{tr}}:=\inf\left\{T\in\mathbb N_0: B(\mathcal G,n,x^0)\psi(t)\leq A\phi(t)\ \text{for every }t\geq T\right\}.\] This horizon is finite. For every \(t\geq T_{\mathrm{tr}}\), the network-dependent term is no larger than the centralized-scale term. Poor connectivity or larger initial disagreement may increase \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\) without changing the leading asymptotic scale.
assumptions_latex: \(E_t\geq0\), \(\phi(t)>0\) eventually, and \(\psi(t)\geq0\).
\(A>0\) and \(B(\mathcal G,n,x^0)\) is finite and nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The horizon \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\) is finite, and \(B(\mathcal G,n,x^0)\psi(t)\leq A\phi(t)\) for every \(t\geq T_{\mathrm{tr}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error decomposition separating centralized decay from pre-asymptotic network effects.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a distributed method on graph \(G\), let \(E_k(G)\) denote its error and let \(r_k\) be a target asymptotic envelope. Let \(\theta(G)\) collect topology, population, mixing, delay, and initialization parameters.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a performance-description object for pre-asymptotic behavior, not a convergence theorem for a particular algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a tolerance factor \(C>0\), the network-dependent transient length is \(K_{\mathrm{tr}}(G;C)=\inf\{K\in\mathbb N:\ E_k(G)\le Cr_k\text{ for every }k\ge K\}\), with value \(+\infty\) if the set is empty. A transient theory is a family of valid bounds on \(E_k(G)\) or \(K_{\mathrm{tr}}(G;C)\) that displays its dependence on \(\theta(G)\). A decomposition \(E_k(G)\le Cr_k+T_k(\theta(G))\), where \(T_k\) dominates initially and becomes no larger than the target envelope after a parameter-dependent time, is a canonical transient description.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The transient length is the first index after which the distributed error remains below a fixed multiple of the target asymptotic envelope. Network-dependent transient theory records how this burn-in or the pre-asymptotic error depends on graph topology, number of agents, initialization, delays, or mixing quality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[K_{\mathrm{tr}}(G;C):=\inf\{K\in\mathbb N:\forall k\ge K,\ E_k(G)\le Cr_k\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a decomposition \(E_k(G)\le Cr_k+T_k(\theta(G))\), one may define the crossover index \(K_\times(G)=\inf\{k:T_k(\theta(G))\le Cr_k\}\).
special_cases_latex: With geometric mixing \(T_k=A(G)\sigma(G)^k\), \(0<\sigma(G)<1\), the transient is controlled by the mixing factor and initial amplitude.
immediate_consequences_latex: A graph-independent leading rate can coexist with an unbounded transient length over a poorly connected graph class.
boundary_notes: The definition requires an eventual-for-all-indices condition, not merely a single crossing of the envelope.
Oscillatory or nonmonotone errors may make the first hitting time smaller than the transient length.

notation.meaning: Persistent burn-in index for the target envelope.

children.top_down_role: Rates organized by objective, network, and oracle regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Deterministic Gradient-Tracking Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smooth strongly convex deterministic gradient tracking converges geometrically for a sufficiently small network-dependent constant stepsize.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\) be fixed, symmetric, and doubly stochastic, with \(\rho=\|W-n^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\|_2<1\). Suppose every \(f_i\) has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex. For correctly initialized deterministic gradient tracking, there is a variant-dependent threshold \(\bar\alpha(L,\mu,\rho)>0\) such that, for \(0<\alpha<\bar\alpha\), constants \(C<\infty\) and \(q\in(0,1)\) satisfy \[\|X^k-\mathbf1(x^*)^\top\|_F^2+\|Y^k\|_F^2\le Cq^k.\] Hence this squared-error metric reaches \(\varepsilon\) in \(O(\log(1/\varepsilon))\) communication rounds.
assumptions_latex: The fixed balanced network has disagreement contraction \(\rho<1\).
Every local gradient is \(L\)-Lipschitz and the aggregate objective is \(\mu\)-strongly convex.
The tracker is correctly initialized and the constant stepsize is below the selected recursion's stability threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E_k\le Cq^k,\qquad K_\varepsilon=O(\log(1/\varepsilon)).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed balanced-network rate family for smooth strongly convex aggregate optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Nonconvex Stationarity Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smooth nonconvex deterministic gradient tracking has a best-iterate order-one-over-K squared stationarity and consensus rate under stable mixing and stepsize conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\) is bounded below, every \(f_i\) has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, the fixed balanced network contracts disagreement, and deterministic gradient tracking uses correct initialization and a sufficiently small constant stepsize. Standard Lyapunov analyses give \[\min_{0\le k<K}\left(\|\nabla F(\bar x^k)\|^2+\|X^k-\mathbf1(\bar x^k)^\top\|_F^2\right)\le\frac{C}{K}.\] Thus this squared stationarity-consensus metric reaches \(\varepsilon\) in \(O(1/\varepsilon)\) rounds.
assumptions_latex: The aggregate objective is bounded below.
All local gradients are Lipschitz continuous.
Mixing contracts disagreement, initialization is exact, and the stepsize satisfies the selected method's stability restriction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{0\le k<K}E_k^{\mathrm{stat}}\le C/K.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-iterate deterministic stationarity and consensus rate on a fixed balanced network.

notation.meaning: squared aggregate-gradient norm plus primal disagreement

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Tracking Convergence-Rate Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A common representation separating optimization, consensus, and stationarity rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X^k=((x_1^k)^{\mathsf T},\ldots,(x_n^k)^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{nd}\), let \(\bar x^k=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^k\), and let \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\). When \(F^*=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^d}F(x)\) is finite, convex-objective rate measures include
\[
E_{\mathrm{opt}}(k)=\mathbb E[F(\bar x^k)-F^*],
\qquad
E_{\mathrm{con}}(k)=\mathbb E\lVert X^k-\mathbf1\otimes\bar x^k\rVert^2.
\]
For a smooth nonconvex objective and an integer \(K\geq1\), a stationarity measure is
\[
S_K=K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\mathbb E\lVert\nabla F(\bar x^k)\rVert^2.
\]
A rate family specifies bounds on one or more of these quantities as functions of iteration count, objective regularity, oracle noise, and network contraction; geometric, polynomial, and noise-floor bounds are distinct regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient-tracking rates can be organized by objective error, consensus disagreement, or averaged stationarity, together with their objective, network, and oracle assumptions.
assumptions_latex: For objective-error rates, \(F^*=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^d}F(x)>-\infty\).
For \(S_K\), the objective \(F\) is differentiable and \(K\geq1\).
The expectations cover all algorithmic and oracle randomness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A rate claim is identified by a bound on \(E_{\mathrm{opt}}(k)\), \(E_{\mathrm{con}}(k)\), or \(S_K\), together with the regime assumptions under which that bound holds.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(n\) agents minimize \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\) over \(\mathbb R^d\). Let \(x_i^k\) be agent \(i\)'s primal iterate, \(y_i^k\) its gradient tracker, \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}F\), and \(W^k\) the communication operator.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A taxonomy-level definition for deterministic or stochastic gradient-tracking methods; it defines how rates are indexed rather than asserting that a particular rate holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A gradient-tracking convergence-rate family is a collection \(\{\mathcal R_{\mathsf o,\mathsf n,\mathsf q}\}\) indexed by an objective regime \(\mathsf o\), network regime \(\mathsf n\), and oracle regime \(\mathsf q\). Each member specifies an error functional \(E_k\), constants independent of \(k\), and a bound valid for every \(k\ge0\), such as \(E_k\le C\rho^k E_0\) with \(0<\rho<1\), \(E_k\le C(k+1)^{-p}\), or \(\min_{0\le t<k}E_t\le Ck^{-p}+\varepsilon_{\mathsf q}\). The error may combine optimality, consensus, and tracking components: \(E_k=a\|\bar x^k-x^\star\|^2+b\|X^k-\mathbf1(\bar x^k)^\top\|_F^2+c\|Y^k-\mathbf1(\bar y^k)^\top\|_F^2\), where \(a,b,c\ge0\) are not all zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gradient-tracking convergence-rate family groups iteration-indexed error bounds by three regimes: objective assumptions, network assumptions, and oracle assumptions. Each family member identifies an error combining optimization, consensus, and tracking discrepancies and gives either a geometric, sublinear, or residual-floor bound with constants independent of the iteration counter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R_{\mathsf o,\mathsf n,\mathsf q}\) is defined by its regime triple, error functional \(E_k\), and a quantified bound for all \(k\ge0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a nonnegative error sequence, \(E_k\le C\rho^kE_0\) is equivalently an \(R\)-linear bound with contraction factor at most \(\rho\).
special_cases_latex: Strongly convex smooth deterministic problems commonly use geometric-form members; convex or nonconvex regimes commonly use ergodic or stationarity-form members.
immediate_consequences_latex: The family distinguishes network dependence in \(C\) and \(\rho\) from oracle-induced residual terms \(\varepsilon_{\mathsf q}\).
boundary_notes: This definition does not claim that every combination of regimes admits every displayed rate.
A precise theorem must separately state connectivity, smoothness, stepsize, and noise hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Diffusion Bias-Correction Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With smooth strongly convex objectives and a small constant step, deterministic exact diffusion converges linearly to the exact consensual optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let every \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, smooth, and strongly convex, and let the fixed undirected communication graph admit a symmetric doubly stochastic matrix \(A\) with \(\ker(I-A)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\). For deterministic exact diffusion with a sufficiently small constant step size \(\alpha>0\), there exist \(C<\infty\) and \(\rho\in(0,1)\) such that \[\|X^k-\mathbf1(x^\star)^\top\|^2\le C\rho^k,\] where \(x^\star\) is the unique minimizer of \(n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\). Hence the limiting consensus point is \(x^\star\), with no nonzero steady-state network bias.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is smooth and strongly convex.
\(A=A^\top\), \(A\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and \(\ker(I-A)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\).
\(\alpha>0\) satisfies the method-specific stability bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\|X^k-\mathbf1(x^\star)^\top\|^2\le C\rho^k\longrightarrow0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic convergence statement emphasizing removal of constant-step network bias.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: linear exact convergence is the canonical strongly-convex deterministic result

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind is correct for this convergence leaf, but a linear-convergence theorem cannot be accepted from standard-field rationale alone. The exact admissible step-size and any additional eigenvalue, weighting, initialization, or objective assumptions must be taken from a method-specific theorem. No supporting source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(W^k\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\) be the stacked exact-diffusion iterates for minimizing \(F(x)=\sum_i f_i(x)\), and let \(W^\star=\mathbf1(x^\star)^\top\) for a solution \(x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the convergence property that distinguishes exact diffusion from neighborhood convergence; it is not a theorem supplying sufficient hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact-diffusion trajectory has bias-correction convergence when its optimization and disagreement errors vanish at a persistent stepsize: \(\lim_{k\to\infty}\|\bar w^k-x^\star\|=0\) and \(\lim_{k\to\infty}\|W^k-\mathbf1(\bar w^k)^\top\|_F=0\). Equivalently, \(W^k\to W^\star\). In a stochastic constant-stepsize regime, the corresponding mean-square property is separated into a noise term and a network-bias term: bias correction means the deterministic network-heterogeneity contribution to \(\limsup_k n^{-1}\mathbb E\|W^k-W^\star\|_F^2\) is zero, although an oracle-noise floor may remain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bias-correction convergence means that deterministic exact-diffusion iterates reach the common optimizer rather than a network-dependent neighborhood despite a nonvanishing stepsize. In stochastic operation, it means the persistent error contains no deterministic network-heterogeneity bias, although sampling noise can still cause a nonzero mean-square floor.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strong duality, network connectivity, bounded residuals, and standard diminishing stepsizes, local prices agree at a dual optimum and ergodic allocations become optimal and balanced.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Saddle-Residual Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ergodic saddle gap is bounded by the centralized cumulative constant plus accumulated network errors, divided by the iteration count. Summable errors preserve an order-one-over-K rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\ge 1\), let \(\bar z^K=K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}z^k\), and define \(G_Z(w)=\sup_{z\in Z}\langle F(z),w-z\rangle\). If, for every \(z\in Z\), \(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\langle F(z^k),z^k-z\rangle\le C+\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\varepsilon_k\), then
\[
G_Z(\bar z^K)\le \frac{C+\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\varepsilon_k}{K}.
\]
If \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty\), then \(G_Z(\bar z^K)=O(K^{-1})\). If only \(K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\varepsilon_k\to0\), then \(G_Z(\bar z^K)\to0\).
assumptions_latex: The set \(Z\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) is nonempty, compact, and convex, and contains a solution.
The operator \(F:Z\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is monotone, and \(z^k\in Z\) for every \(k\).
The constant satisfies \(C\ge0\), the errors satisfy \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\), and the displayed cumulative inequality holds for every integer \(K\ge1\) and every \(z\in Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(K\ge1\), \(G_Z(\bar z^K)\le\bigl(C+\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\varepsilon_k\bigr)/K\); summable errors yield \(G_Z(\bar z^K)=O(K^{-1})\).

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Convergence under Graph Connectivity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a connected graph, incidence-based agreement is exact. If a finite-dimensional distributed primal-dual update is averaged and its fixed points are exactly KKT points, every iterate sequence converges to a consensual primal-dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite connected undirected graph, let \(\mathcal X\) be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space, and let \(K\) be an oriented incidence operator lifted to \(\mathcal X^{|V|}\), so that \[\ker K=\{(x_1,\ldots,x_{|V|}):x_1=\cdots=x_{|V|}\}.\] Suppose a distributed primal-dual splitting on a finite-dimensional product space \(\mathcal H\) is represented by \[w^{k+1}=Tw^k,\] where \(T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\) is averaged in an inner product induced by a positive-definite operator and \(\operatorname{Fix}(T)\ne\varnothing\). Suppose a decoding map \(D\) maps the fixed-point equations exactly to the KKT system of the network saddle problem, including \(Kx=0\). Then, for every \(w^0\in\mathcal H\), the sequence \((w^k)\) converges to some \(w^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}(T)\); the decoded primal component reaches agreement, and \(D(w^\star)\) satisfies the network saddle conditions.

\(\mathcal H\) is finite-dimensional.
\(T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\) is averaged in a positive-definite metric and \(\operatorname{Fix}(T)\ne\varnothing\).
The decoding map \(D\) identifies the fixed-point system of \(T\) with the network KKT system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w^k\to w^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}(T)\), the decoded primal component satisfies \(Kx^\star=0\), and \(D(w^\star)\) is a primal-dual solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Primal-Dual Stepsize Conditions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive local primal and dual stepsizes satisfy the stated stability condition when the norm of the diagonally scaled network-coupling operator is strictly below one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\) and \(\mathcal Y\) be finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces and consider the convex saddle problem \[\min_{x\in\mathcal X}\max_{y\in\mathcal Y}\; f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y),\] where \(K:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y\) is linear. \(f\) and \(g^*\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(K:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y\) is linear.
\(T\) and \(\Sigma\) are block-diagonal and strongly positive.

Primal–Dual Feasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible primal pair, a multiplier, and matching local subgradients certify optimality when the primal and stationarity residuals all vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\), \(\mathcal Z\), and \(\mathcal Y\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(A:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y\) and \(B:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y\) be bounded linear operators, and consider \[\min_{x\in\mathcal X,\,z\in\mathcal Z} f(x)+g(z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax+Bz=c.\] A tuple \((x,z,y,s_x,s_z)\) is an exact primal-dual feasibility certificate when \[s_x\in\partial f(x),\qquad s_z\in\partial g(z),\qquad Ax+Bz-c=0,\] and \[s_x+A^*y=0,\qquad s_z+B^*y=0.\] These relations are the KKT conditions. Under the stated convexity and strong-duality assumptions, they certify that \((x,z)\) is primal optimal and \(y\) is dual optimal.

Strong duality holds for the linear constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Edgewise endpoint differences form a directly verifiable residual. On a connected graph, its vanishing is equivalent to every agent holding the same decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite connected undirected graph with an arbitrary orientation, let \(D\in\mathbb R^{|E|\times|V|}\) be its oriented edge-node incidence matrix, and let \(x=(x_i)_{i\in V}\in(\mathbb R^d)^{|V|}\) be the stacked local decisions. Connectivity gives \[\ker(D\otimes I_d)=\{\mathbf 1\otimes v:v\in\mathbb R^d\},\] so \(r_{\mathrm{con}}=0\) certifies global agreement.

\(D\in\mathbb R^{|E|\times|V|}\) is an oriented edge-node incidence matrix of \(G\).
Every local decision belongs to \(\mathbb R^d\).

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Feasibility–Agreement Residuals
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The joint residual combines affine-feasibility violation and network disagreement, and it vanishes exactly when the affine constraints and componentwise consensus both hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,d,p\in\mathbb N\), let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected communication graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \(B\in\mathbb R^{|E|\times m}\) be an oriented incidence matrix of \(G\). knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(n\) agents hold states \(x_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\) and minimize \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\). Let \(Q_{ij}^k\) denote the possibly randomized compression map applied to the message sent from agent \(j\) to agent \(i\), and set \(\bar x^k=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A property of a specified distributed algorithm-compressor pair; the definition separates optimization and consensus requirements and is not itself a rate theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A compressed distributed algorithm is convergent to a solution \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}F\) if its iterates, generated using messages \(Q_{ij}^k(m_{ij}^k)\), satisfy both optimization convergence and network agreement. Almost-sure convergence means \(\bar x^k\to x^\star\) and \(\max_i\|x_i^k-\bar x^k\|\to0\) almost surely. Mean-square convergence replaces these limits by \(\mathbb E\|\bar x^k-x^\star\|^2\to0\) and \(\mathbb E[n^{-1}\sum_i\|x_i^k-\bar x^k\|^2]\to0\). Convergence to an error neighborhood of radius \(r\) means the corresponding limsup is at most \(r^2\), rather than zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compressed distributed convergence means that an algorithm using compressed messages simultaneously approaches a minimizer of the aggregate objective and reaches agreement among agents. The mode of convergence must be stated explicitly, such as almost sure or mean square. If the limiting error is nonzero, the property is convergence to a neighborhood rather than exact convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x^k\to x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}F\quad\text{and}\quad\max_i\|x_i^k-\bar x^k\|\to0\) in the declared convergence mode.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In mean square, agreement can be written as \(n^{-1}\sum_i\mathbb E\|x_i^k-\bar x^k\|^2\to0\).
special_cases_latex: Exact communication is the special case \(Q_{ij}^k(v)=v\).
Neighborhood convergence permits \(\limsup_k\mathbb E\|\bar x^k-x^\star\|^2\le r^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Exact optimization convergence plus agreement implies \(x_i^k\to x^\star\) for every agent in the same mode.
boundary_notes: Objective-value convergence alone does not define agent agreement.
The compressor assumptions and algorithmic update must be specified before this property can become a guarantee.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimized Convex Rate under Independent Unbiased Compression
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent unbiased compression preserves the inverse-square-root convex rate, inflating its constant by the square root of the averaged compressor-variance factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the assumptions of Unbiased-Compressed Distributed Subgradient Bound, suppose \(\|x_0-x^*\|\le D\) and choose \[\alpha_k=\frac{D}{G\sqrt{(1+\omega/n)K}},\qquad 0\le k<K.\] Then \(\bar x_K=K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}x_k\) and \[\mathbb E[f(\bar x_K)-f(x^*)]\le\frac{DG\sqrt{1+\omega/n}}{\sqrt K}.\] Consequently, expected objective error at most \(\varepsilon\) is guaranteed when \[K\ge\frac{D^2G^2(1+\omega/n)}{\varepsilon^2}.\]
assumptions_latex: All assumptions of Unbiased-Compressed Distributed Subgradient Bound hold.
The horizon \(K\) is fixed when the constant stepsize is selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[f(\bar x_K)-f(x^*)]\le DG\sqrt{1+\omega/n}/\sqrt K.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbiased-Compressed Distributed Subgradient Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronized distributed projected subgradient descent retains its convex ergodic bound, with independent unbiased compression adding averaged variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nf_i on a closed convex set C, let x^*\in\arg\min_C f, and choose g_{i,k}\in\partial f_i(x_k) with \|g_{i,k}\|\le G. Suppose q_{i,k}=Q_{i,k}(g_{i,k}) are conditionally independent across workers and satisfy \mathbb E_kq_{i,k}=g_{i,k} and \mathbb E_k\|q_{i,k}-g_{i,k}\|^2\le\omega\|g_{i,k}\|^2. For \[x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha_k\bar q_k),\quad \bar q_k=n^{-1}\sum_iq_{i,k},\quad \bar x_K=\frac{\sum_{k<K}\alpha_kx_k}{\sum_{k<K}\alpha_k},\] \[\mathbb E[f(\bar x_K)-f(x^*)]\le\frac{\|x_0-x^*\|^2+G^2(1+\omega/n)\sum_{k<K}\alpha_k^2}{2\sum_{k<K}\alpha_k}.\]
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is convex with subgradients bounded by G on C.
Compressors are conditionally unbiased and conditionally independent across workers.
A minimizer exists and all workers use the common iterate.

knowledge_statements.title: Compressed Convex Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An abstract convex convergence result for unbiased compressed stochastic subgradient descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be convex with a minimizer \(x^\star\), and consider \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha_k Q(g^k)\). Suppose \(\mathbb E[g^k\mid x^k]\in\partial F(x^k)\), \(\mathbb E[\|g^k\|^2\mid x^k]\leq G^2\), and the compressor obeys \(\mathbb E[Q(v)\mid v]=v\) and \(\mathbb E\|Q(v)-v\|^2\leq\omega\|v\|^2\). If \(\alpha_k>0\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\), then \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}F(x^k)=F(x^\star)\) almost surely; standard bounded-iterate conditions give convergence to the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unbiased compression with bounded relative variance preserves asymptotic convex subgradient convergence under square-summable but nonsummable step sizes.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is convex, attains its minimum, and stochastic subgradients have bounded conditional second moment
\(Q\) is conditionally unbiased with relative variance parameter \(\omega<\infty\)
\(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}F(x^k)=F(x^\star)\) almost surely.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let each \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, let \(F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\), assume \(X^\star=\operatorname*{argmin}F\ne\varnothing\), and let \(x_i^k\) be iterates produced using compressed communications. Write \(F^\star=\min F\) and \(\bar x^k=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i^k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A compressed distributed method has convex convergence for an output sequence \(\widehat x^K\) if the compression-driven iterates satisfy \(F(\widehat x^K)-F^\star\to0\) and their consensus residual tends to zero in a declared deterministic or probabilistic mode. For mean convergence this is \(\mathbb E[F(\widehat x^K)-F^\star]\to0\) together with \(\mathbb E[n^{-1}\sum_i\|x_i^K-\bar x^K\|^2]\to0\). If boundedness and lower semicontinuity are part of the selected regime, solution-set convergence may instead be recorded as \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x^K,X^\star)^2]\to0\). The output may be the last average \(\bar x^K\) or a stated weighted average of iterates.

special_cases_latex: Ergodic convergence uses \(\widehat x^K=(\sum_{k=0}^{K}a_k\bar x^k)/(\sum_{k=0}^{K}a_k)\) for declared weights \(a_k>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Staleness Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractive fixed-point iteration converges despite asynchrony when delays and gaps between component updates are uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) be complete under a block-maximum norm, and let \(F:X\to X\) satisfy \(\lVert F(x)-F(z)\rVert\le q\lVert x-z\rVert\) for some \(q\in[0,1)\). At event \(k\), selected components replace their values by the corresponding components of \(F\) evaluated at a mixed-time vector whose timestamps lie in \([k-\tau,k]\); unselected components are unchanged. If every component is selected at least once in every \(B\) consecutive events, then the asynchronous iterates converge to the unique fixed point \(x^*\) of \(F\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is complete and \(F\) is a contraction with modulus \(q<1\).
Every read is at most \(\tau<\infty\) events old.
Every component is updated within each window of \(B<\infty\) events.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{k\to\infty}x^k=x^*\), where \(F(x^*)=x^*\).

Delay-Dependent Convergence Rates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A delay bound of τ slows the worst-case contraction exponent and event complexity by a factor of at most τ+1.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:X\to X\) be a contraction with modulus \(q\in(0,1)\) and fixed point \(x^*\). Consider
\[
x^{k+1}=F(x^{k-d_k}),\qquad 0\le d_k\le\min\{\tau,k\}.
\]
Then
\[
\lVert x^k-x^*\rVert\le q^{\lceil k/(\tau+1)\rceil}\lVert x^0-x^*\rVert.
\]
Consequently, achieving \(\lVert x^k-x^*\rVert\le\varepsilon\) is guaranteed after at most
\[
(\tau+1)\left\lceil\frac{\log(\lVert x^0-x^*\rVert/\varepsilon)}{-\log q}\right\rceil
\]
events, for \(0<\varepsilon<\lVert x^0-x^*\rVert\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is complete and \(F\) is a \(q\)-contraction.
\(0\le d_k\le\min\{\tau,k\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated error and event-complexity bounds hold for every admissible delay sequence.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Speedup Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel speedup is near-linear while delay increases the required update count by only a worker-independent constant factor relative to the zero-delay serial baseline.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K(\tau,\varepsilon)\) be the number of update events required for accuracy \(\varepsilon\) when staleness is bounded by \(\tau\). Suppose \(p\) workers process \(p\) events per unit time with negligible overhead and that the one-worker baseline has \(\tau(1)=0\). Define
\[
T_p(\varepsilon)=\frac{K(\tau(p),\varepsilon)}{p},\qquad T_1(\varepsilon)=K(0,\varepsilon),\qquad S_p(\varepsilon)=\frac{T_1(\varepsilon)}{T_p(\varepsilon)}.
\]
A worker range is a near-linear speedup regime with constant \(C\ge1\) when
\[
K(\tau(p),\varepsilon)\le C K(0,\varepsilon)
\]
throughout that range. Then \(S_p(\varepsilon)\ge p/C\).
assumptions_latex: Workers sustain aggregate throughput \(p\) updates per unit time.
Scheduling and communication overhead are excluded from \(T_p\).
The one-worker baseline satisfies \(\tau(1)=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Stale-Update Penalties
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stale-gradient error is at most the smoothness constant times the accumulated iterate movement since the gradient was computed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) have \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, and let an event use the stale gradient \(g^k=\nabla f(x^{k-d_k})\), where \(0\le d_k\le\tau\). Then
\[
\lVert g^k-\nabla f(x^k)\rVert
\le L\lVert x^{k-d_k}-x^k\rVert
\le L\sum_{t=k-d_k}^{k-1}\lVert x^{t+1}-x^t\rVert.
\]
Thus staleness contributes an error controlled by the cumulative motion during the omitted events; it vanishes whenever the sum of those intervening step lengths vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(\lVert\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(z)\rVert\le L\lVert x-z\rVert\) for all \(x,z\in\mathbb{R}^d\).
\(0\le d_k\le\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert g^k-\nabla f(x^k)\rVert\le L\sum_{t=k-d_k}^{k-1}\lVert x^{t+1}-x^t\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lipschitz bound on gradient error caused by a delayed iterate.

knowledge_statements.title: Speedup Saturation Limits
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When staleness and delay-induced work both grow linearly with worker count, idealized parallel speedup remains uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K_0(\varepsilon)>0\) be the serial update count and suppose an asynchronous method with \(p\) workers requires
\[
K_p(\varepsilon)\ge c\bigl(1+\tau(p)\bigr)K_0(\varepsilon)
\]
for some \(c>0\). Under ideal throughput \(p\), its speedup is \(S_p=pK_0(\varepsilon)/K_p(\varepsilon)\). If the induced staleness satisfies \(\tau(p)\ge a(p-1)\) for some \(a>0\), then
\[
S_p\le\frac{p}{c(1+a(p-1))}\le\frac{1}{c\min\{1,a\}}.
\]
Hence increasing worker count cannot produce unbounded speedup in this regime.
assumptions_latex: \(K_p(\varepsilon)\ge c(1+\tau(p))K_0(\varepsilon)\).
\(\tau(p)\ge a(p-1)\) with \(a,c>0\).
Aggregate processing capacity is at most \(p\) updates per unit time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_p\le 1/(c\min\{1,a\})\) for every integer \(p\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worker-independent speedup ceiling when delay-induced work grows linearly with concurrency.
